title: Show HN: Run Google DataProc cluster on your local
author: jaysen_apache
raw_text:
Google does not provide official docker image for developers or AI agents to run dataproc cluster locally. so everybody need to spin up for even dev/CI testing,etc..now you or your AI agent can: 
docker run --rm agentcloud/dataproc:3.0.0-debian13 self-testsaves time and cost.it basically packages the same component version and make the hadoop and spark to developer.Here are docker images for other dataproc versions:https://hub.docker.com/r/agentcloud/dataproc/tagshere is full blog for more use-cases: https://local.cloud/blog/run-dataproc-locally-docker/
summary: This item introduces a docker image that lets you run a Google DataProc cluster locally on your machine. DataProc is Google Cloud's managed service for big data processing, primarily using Apache Hadoop and Spark. Traditionally, developing and testing applications for DataProc required spinning up a cloud cluster, which could be slow and costly for iterative development. This local solution provides a convenient way to simulate the DataProc environment, allowing you to develop, test, and debug your Spark and Hadoop jobs without cloud dependencies. It helps save time and money during the development and continuous integration phases. You could try pulling the docker image and running a basic spark word count example to see it in action.
why: Test big data pipelines locally, saving time and cloud costs.

title: pipeshub-ai/pipeshub-ai
author: pipeshub-ai
raw_text: PipesHub is an open-source platform for securely connecting enterprise knowledge to AI. Give AI agents trusted context and your team permission-aware search with verified citations across your business systems. agent agents ai docker enterprise-search fastapi glean graphrag knowledge-graph langchain langgraph mcp notion ollama python rag retrieval-augmented-generation self-hosted slack workplace-ai
summary:
pipeshub is an open-source platform designed to securely connect enterprise knowledge to ai. its goal is to provide ai agents with trusted context and allow teams to perform searches with verified citations across their business systems, while respecting permissions. this platform integrates with various data sources, leveraging techniques like rag and knowledge graphs to ensure accuracy and relevance. it's also built to be self-hosted, offering flexibility and control. the project touches upon full-stack development, using tools like fastapi and docker, showing how to build robust ai solutions for real-world business environments.

you could look into its architecture to understand how it combines rag, agents, and enterprise data sources effectively.
why: connects enterprise knowledge to ai agents securely, crucial for real-world ai deployment.
